checks.invariant: A PermissionMap read-only override must refuse every write-gated op whose effect lands on a row at or beneath the override, including subtree-shaped ops (cascade delete, move, copy, sweep, restore) addressed at a writable ancestor or a writable destination
checks.result: Violated. With read_write(read=['/dir/frozen']) on the root, a non-system caller (alice) is correctly refused write/delete/move at /dir/frozen/*, but delete('/dir') trashes /dir/frozen/ledger.md, sweep('/dir') purges it, move('/dir','/moved') + write('/moved/frozen/ledger.md') + move('/moved','/dir') replaces the locked body with 'TAMPERED', and copy('/stage','/dir') or move('/stage','/dir') plants attacker content at /dir/frozen/ledger.md in one call. check_writable resolves only the addressed path (longest prefix that covers it), never overrides strictly beneath it; the router does apply a subtree rule for bind sites (_busy_guard subtree=True) but not for permission overrides.

checks.invariant: parents=True on write/mkdir must not revive tombstoned or create rows in a read-only region beyond what design intends
checks.result: With read_only(write=['/a/b/c']), write('/a/b/c/new.md', parents=True) mints empty directory rows /a and /a/b inside the read-only default (direct mkdir('/a') is refused read_only). With a tombstoned read-only ancestor, the write is refused not_found and nothing revives. Minting of brand-new ancestors is the documented carve-out that lets a writable hole exist in a read-only mount; recorded as hardening, not a finding.

checks.invariant: Every write-shaped verb runs _gate_entry (capability minus deny_ops, reserved grammar, composed PermissionMap layers) before dispatch
checks.result: Holds. _route_single (base.py:1748), _dispatch_grouped_observations, _route_two_path (2535-2537, both endpoints for move, dest plus read-grammar src for copy), _route_entry_batch, _route_edge_batch (both endpoints) and _route_grant (2039) all call _gate_entry; WRITE_GATED_OPS = MUTATING_OPS | GRANT_WRITE_OPS covers write/edit/delete/restore/sweep/mkdir/mkedge/rmedge/move/copy/grant/revoke/posture/add_member/remove_member. run is EXEC (not write-gated) but no in-tree storage implements SupportsRun, and deny_ops can mask it. caps = declared_caps - deny_ops is recomputed whole on every meta replacement (MountMeta.__post_init__); read ops cannot be masked by design.

checks.invariant: The /.vfs/X -> /X metadata alias must not loosen a read-only rule
checks.result: Holds. _permission_candidates keeps the canonical /.vfs path first and the alias only wins when its matched rule prefix is strictly longer; a read rule on /X therefore also tightens /.vfs/X, and a writable hole on /X extends to /.vfs/X by design (pinned by test_writable_hole_reaches_its_metadata_projection). /.vfs rows are ordinary stored rows in the database backend, so the alias grants no reach into another path's derived metadata.

checks.invariant: remount or a deeper bind cannot loosen a parent's map
checks.result: Holds. _permission_layers walks every binding whose path prefixes the target (root included, rel rebased per layer) and check_writable_composed returns the first denial, so a loosened child map is still gated by every ancestor layer. remount and bind are host/operator control-plane methods, not routed verbs.

checks.invariant: A session or sync facade call runs with exactly the bound authority
checks.result: Holds. AsyncSession has no **kwargs and every one of the 25 verbs forwards authority=self._authority; sync.Session wraps an AsyncSession and forwards through it; VirtualFileSystem twins pass the caller's authority argument unchanged. Authority is a frozen value, re-derived per call, so a close() race leaves no stale or swapped authority (an in-flight verb finishes with the same immutable authority it started with).

checks.invariant: No spelling of a path (relative, whitespace-padded segment, '.', '..', doubled slash, NFD vs NFC, tab) can pass the router's map or reserved grammar yet address a protected row, a reserved tree, or another mount's prefix
checks.result: Holds. 18 spellings against read-only overrides (/dir/frozen, an NFD-declared /café/ro), a read-only mount at /m, /.vfs and the trash view all canonicalized to the same Path and were refused read_only or invalid; the protected bodies stayed 'LOCKED'. normalize_path is applied once at the gate and to PermissionMap override prefixes alike, and storage receives the branded canonical Path.

checks.invariant: Reserved grammar holds in both global and mount-local coordinates, and mount boundaries refuse cross-mount pairs
checks.result: Holds. resolve_path(mutation=True) checks the global path and _gate_entry re-runs check_reserved_path on the mount-local rel with head_ok only for sweep; mount paths may not contain a .vfs segment (_normalize_mount_path); move/copy and mkedge/rmedge refuse endpoints on different bindings (cross_mount) before dispatch; bind-site and bind-containing regions are busy for delete/restore/sweep/move/copy dest. Rebase overflow raises in Path.with_mount and is classified per row; the gate's own rebase uses a rel derived from a lawful full path, so it cannot overflow.

checks.invariant: Rows from a shallower storage beneath a deeper bind, including grant rows carried as an extra, are not served as the shallower mount's answer
checks.result: Holds for the security boundary. _shadow_filter drops observations only, but the grants extra lists rows on the addressed path and its ancestors only (DatabaseStorage.grants), and a path beneath a deeper bind routes to the deeper binding, so a shallow grants answer cannot name a prefix inside a deeper mount. Observation/entry/edge batch rows each route by their own path to their own binding.

checks.invariant: Router (case-sensitive, NFC) and storage compare paths identically
checks.result: Holds on supported engines: BytewiseString pins collation C on Postgres, Latin1_General_100_BIN2_UTF8 on MSSQL, VARBINARY on the mysql family, SQLite BINARY by default. Oracle and unknown dialects rely on engine defaults (noted as hardening).

candidates.title: Read-only PermissionMap overrides are bypassed by subtree verbs (delete cascade, move, copy, sweep, restore) addressed at a writable ancestor or destination
candidates.description: The router's PermissionMap is documented as the per-prefix write policy enforced at the routing chokepoint before anything dispatches (README.md:127; read_write(read=[...]) reads as 'writable with these read-only holes'). The gate resolves only the exact path a verb addresses. A verb whose effect spans a subtree is therefore checked against the ancestor's rule and never against a read-only override nested beneath it. Any caller with row rights on the ancestor can: trash the read-only rows with delete(ancestor), destroy them permanently with sweep(ancestor), move the ancestor out, edit the formerly read-only file at its new address and move it back, or plant attacker content inside the read-only region in one call with copy/move of a staged tree onto the ancestor. The same router already applies a subtree rule for bind sites (_busy_guard with subtree=True) but not for permission overrides.
candidates.root_cause: check_writable (src/vfs/permissions.py:269-321) resolves the gated rel through PermissionMap._resolve, which matches only overrides whose prefix equals or covers the path (permissions.py:195-196). It never considers overrides lying strictly beneath the path. _gate_entry (base.py:2902) calls check_writable_composed with only the addressed rels for every op, including the subtree-shaped ones (delete, restore, sweep, move src/dest, copy dest), so a read-only rule deeper than the target is invisible to the gate.
candidates.intended_behavior: A read-only override must refuse every write-gated op whose effect lands at or beneath it. For subtree-shaped ops, the gate should refuse with read_only when any layer holds a read rule strictly beneath the target rel (and its /.vfs alias), mirroring how _busy_guard refuses a region that holds a bind site.

trace.description: Caller (anonymous or a named agent) calls delete('/dir'), sweep('/dir'), move('/dir','/moved') or copy/move('/stage','/dir') with its own authority
Single-path verbs gate with write_rels=(terminal.rel,): only the addressed path; the busy guard above (1743) checks bind sites beneath but nothing checks permission rules beneath
move gates (src, dest) and copy gates dest only: the roots of the transferred subtree, not the paths that will be written beneath dest or vacated beneath src
check_writable_composed(self._permission_layers(full), op) is called per addressed rel only
Resolution walks _permission_candidates(rel) (the path and its /.vfs alias) through PermissionMap._resolve
Matches only prefixes that equal or cover the path; '/dir' resolves to the read_write default even though '/dir/frozen' is read-only, so the gate returns None
Storage executes the subtree delete/sweep (and, via base.py:2545, the subtree move/copy), mutating rows under the read-only override

evidence.description: Override loop matches 'normalized == prefix or normalized.startswith(prefix + "/")' only; no check for prefixes beneath the path
_busy_guard does consider the subtree (_bindings_beneath when subtree=True) for bind sites, showing subtree-shaped effects are recognised for mounts but not for permission overrides
_BUSY_GUARDED_OPS = {delete, restore, sweep}: the router's own list of ops that act beneath the addressed site
Per-prefix map documented as enforced at the routing chokepoint before anything dispatches
The only permission-map call site in the gate, invoked with addressed rels only

conditions.description: The operator configured a read-only PermissionMap override nested beneath a writable non-root prefix of the same mount (e.g. read_write(read=['/dir/frozen']), or an explicit nested PermissionMap). A read-only override directly under a mount root is not reachable this way, because the root cannot be deleted or moved and a bind site is busy.

The caller holds row rung read_write on the writable ancestor (for delete/move/sweep/restore) or add/contribute plus read_write on the destination (copy/move). A fresh mount's default posture gives everyone, including anonymous, read_write, so no grant is needed by default.
Rows exist under the read-only override (for delete/move/sweep tampering), or the caller can stage a tree elsewhere and the destination ancestor is absent (copy/move planting).

execution.attacker_perspective: A named non-system agent principal (alice) calling routed verbs on an AsyncVirtualFileSystem whose root InMemoryStorage carries permissions=read_write(read=['/dir/frozen']), with /dir/frozen/ledger.md seeded by the host as 'LOCKED v1'.
payloads: await fs.move(src='/dir', dest='/moved', authority=alice); await fs.write(path='/moved/frozen/ledger.md', content='TAMPERED', authority=alice); await fs.move(src='/moved', dest='/dir', authority=alice)
await fs.write(path='/stage/frozen/ledger.md', content='FORGED', parents=True, authority=alice); await fs.copy(src='/stage', dest='/dir', authority=alice)
await fs.write(path='/stage/frozen/ledger.md', content='FORGED', parents=True, authority=alice); await fs.move(src='/stage', dest='/dir', authority=alice)
instructions: Construct AsyncVirtualFileSystem(storage=InMemoryStorage(), permissions=read_write(read=['/dir/frozen'])) and seed /dir, /dir/frozen and /dir/frozen/ledger.md through the storage as Authority.system().
As control, confirm write/delete/move at /dir/frozen and /dir/frozen/ledger.md by alice classify vfs.read_only.
Run each payload on a fresh filesystem and read /dir/frozen/ledger.md as Authority.system().
Commands: ./tools/sandbox-run.py ./agents/h04-router/scratch .venv/bin/python -I t1_subtree.py and t3_copy.py (SQLite in-memory only, no network).
execution.observed_result: Controls refused with vfs.read_only. delete('/dir') success=True, then read of /dir/frozen/ledger.md -> not_found. sweep('/dir') success=True, row purged (not_found). move-out/write/move-back all success=True and the file content became ['TAMPERED']. copy('/stage','/dir') and move('/stage','/dir') success=True and /dir/frozen/ledger.md content became ['FORGED'].

remediation.strategy: Treat delete, restore, sweep, move and copy as subtree-shaped in the permission gate: in addition to resolving the addressed rel, refuse when any layer's map holds a 'read' override strictly beneath that rel (or beneath its /.vfs alias). Apply it to move's src and dest and to copy's dest. This mirrors the bind-site busy guard. Add a regression test with read_write(read=['/dir/frozen']) asserting delete('/dir'), sweep('/dir'), restore('/dir'), move('/dir','/x'), move('/stage','/dir') and copy('/stage','/dir') each classify read_only with no storage call recorded.

code_changes.fixed_code:
# Mutations whose effect reaches beneath the addressed path.
_SUBTREE_OPS: frozenset[Op] = frozenset({"delete", "restore", "sweep", "move", "copy"})

# in _gate_entry:
            err = check_writable_composed(self._permission_layers(full), op, subtree=op in _SUBTREE_OPS)

likelihood.reason: Needs an operator map with a read-only override nested under a writable non-root prefix (an advertised PermissionMap pattern) and a caller with row rights on the ancestor; a fresh mount's default posture already gives everyone read_write. delete, move and copy are ordinary agent verbs.

impact.reason: Integrity and availability of data the operator marked read-only, within one mount: content can be replaced or planted (move/copy), trashed (delete) or irrecoverably purged (sweep). Row-level grants still apply, so no cross-principal read and no escape across mounts.

confidence.reason: Reproduced end to end through the public router verbs on InMemoryStorage with matched refused controls; the source shows the gate never consults overrides beneath the addressed path.

hardening: write/mkdir with parents=True mint brand-new ancestor directory rows inside a read-only region (read_only(write=['/a/b/c']) lets write('/a/b/c/new.md', parents=True) create /a and /a/b although mkdir('/a') is refused). This is the documented carve-out that lets a writable hole exist; tombstoned ancestors are not revived. Consider gating minted ancestors by the map, or documenting that empty ancestor directories are exempt.

add_member/remove_member are gated by the PermissionMap only at the caller-chosen path that picks the mount, although membership is mount-wide; a caller can pick a writable carve-out to pass the map. Storage restricts these verbs to the system actor (trusted), so there is no lower-trust impact; consider gating membership at the mount root rel.

BytewiseString pins bytewise collation for Postgres, MSSQL, the mysql family and SQLite, but Oracle and unknown GENERIC dialects use engine-default collation. A case- or accent-insensitive default there would diverge from the router's case-sensitive, NFC PermissionMap prefix match and let '/DIR/frozen/x' address the '/dir/frozen/x' row. Consider refusing or warning on a non-binary path-column collation at first touch.

resolve_path and the pydantic validators pass a branded Path instance through without re-normalizing, so a host that constructs Path._brand on raw input would skip the gate; this is host-only private API today and becomes relevant only if a wire surface ever deserializes into Path directly.
run is an EXEC op that is not write-gated by PermissionMap; no in-tree storage implements SupportsRun, so a future SupportsRun backend that writes should be write-gated or documented as such.
